native_runtime_proof.excerpt:
N  ← ⋕◇∘⊡1 &args
Cr ← -1.5 ×2÷N⇡N
~M {R I Index Cx Cy Iter}
Advance ← M ⊃(+⊃M.Cx(-⊃(˙×M.I)(˙×M.R))|+⊃M.Cy(×2×⊃M.R M.I)|M.Index|M.Cx|M.Cy|+1M.Iter)
~Selection {State Keep}
Selected ← Selection ⊃(∘|⊚ ≤4+⊃(˙×M.R)(˙×M.I))
Prune ← M ⊃(⊏⊃Selection.Keep(M.R Selection.State)|⊏⊃Selection.Keep(M.I Selection.State)|⊏⊃Selection.Keep(M.Index Selection.State)|⊏⊃Selection.Keep(M.Cx Selection.State)|M.Cy Selection.State|M.Iter Selection.State) Selected
Iterate ← Prune Advance
Bits ← ⍜⊏⋅1 ⊃M.Index(⋅↯N 0)
Pack ← ≡/+ ×⊙(¤⇌˜ⁿ2⇡8) ⬚0↯(⌈÷8 N)_8
Row ← &fwa "/dev/stdout" Pack Bits ⍢(Iterate|×⊃(<50M.Iter)(>0⧻M.Index)) M (↯N 0) (↯N 0) (⇡N) Cr ⊙0
&p "P4"
&p $"_ _" N N
≡Row -1 ×2÷N⇡N
native_runtime_proof.conclusion: All 14 application/helper lines are counted. Each exact recurrence updates active state; native Where/Select retain states, coordinates and original pixel identities; one final Under Select restores exact-width bits.

native_runtime_proof.conclusion: The qualified 11 LOC application and its existing actual full measurements remain retained and selected. The recurrence arithmetic, coordinates, byte packing, headers and row traversal are preserved by this additional candidate.
Where turns the ordinary zero/one inside mask into stable surviving row indices.
Native Where scans every mask entry and directly emits its surviving index vector; storage is proportional to selected entries, without a user-function callback per pixel.
Select and Where dispatch directly to the general native array implementations.
Ordinary Select converts the complete selector and dispatches by array datatype.
Native selection gathers all supplied rows in order; each of four state/coordinate vectors is selected with the same stable index vector.
Under Select supports replacing selected rows with a scalar; the documented generic operation writes ones at surviving original pixel indices.
UndoSelect pops replacement, original selector and target then dispatches to the ordinary native indexed update.
UndoSelect validates the ordinary selector, handles duplicate semantics and dispatches the replacement and target by datatype.
The lower-rank scalar replacement path writes the repeated scalar directly at every supplied target index; no pixel-pair membership matrix is built.
Binary64 array arithmetic and scalar broadcasting use the general pervasive implementation; arithmetic is unmodified.
